title: Emotion
description: Style React components with Emotion using the css prop, styled components, and theme composition.

data.text: Emotion is a CSS-in-JS library with two APIs: the `css` prop for one-off styles and `styled` for reusable components. It compiles styles to class names, supports object or template syntax, and works well with TypeScript.

data.caption: Object styles with the css prop
A styled component with prop-driven styles

data.title: Install and configure the JSX factory
data.content: The css prop needs the Emotion JSX runtime; without it the prop is ignored.

data.text: For Next.js, emotion provides a SWC plugin and requires client components (`"use client"`) because styles are generated in the browser. On Vite, the `@vitejs/plugin-react` config with `jsxImportSource: "@emotion/react"` is enough.

data.title: Serialization in Server Components
data.text: CSS-in-JS with a runtime cannot run inside React Server Components. Mark the component with "use client" or switch to a build-time solution such as CSS Modules, vanilla-extract, or Tailwind for server-rendered markup.

terms.definition: Emotion's inline styling API; requires the Emotion JSX runtime (jsxImportSource).
A factory that returns a React component with attached styles.
Emotion deduplicates identical style objects at runtime so repeated renders reuse class names.
Extracting generated styles during server rendering so the first paint is styled.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Mention the runtime cost, the setup requirement for the css prop, and that CSS-in-JS is awkward in React Server Components. Comparing it with build-time options shows judgement.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Emotion offers a css prop and a styled API.
The css prop requires configuring the Emotion JSX runtime.
Runtime CSS-in-JS conflicts with Server Components — mark client components.
styled-components and Emotion are direct competitors; pick one.
data.takeaway: CSS-in-JS buys dynamic styling with a runtime cost — that trade-off is the interview answer.
